system.name: STEVE-1
system.one_liner: Instruction-tuned VPT agent for Minecraft: a CVAE prior turns text into MineCLIP goal embeddings that condition a finetuned VPT policy.

content.variant_note: three tinted panels (MineCLIP, Prior, Policy) wired by embedding strips from the text prompt to mouse and keyboard actions
content.argues: Like unCLIP, two models are enough: a policy that follows MineCLIP visual goal embeddings, and a prior that maps text to such embeddings, so the agent follows text and visual instructions.
content.subject: Frozen MineCLIP encoders, a CVAE prior from text embedding to goal embedding, and a VPT policy conditioned on that goal.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each model of a multi-model method its own tinted dotted-frame panel, and show the interfaces between them as short colour-coded embedding strips so the reader sees which modality each vector comes from.
lessons.suits: Compositional methods built from pretrained parts, such as a prior plus a conditioned decoder or policy, where embeddings are the interface between modules.

evidence: Like unCLIP [48], our approach involves two models.
we train a CVAE [54] to sample MineCLIP visual embeddings given a text prompt.

summary: STEVE-1 turns the VPT Minecraft agent into a text- and image-instructable policy without text-labelled trajectories. Figure 1 draws three tinted dotted-frame panels from left to right. In the green MineCLIP panel (Frozen), a video encoder and a text encoder produce the goal embedding and the text embedding, tied by the CLIP objective. In the yellow Prior panel, a CVAE samples the goal embedding from the text embedding and a Gaussian prior. In the grey Policy panel, three frame ResNets get the goal added at each step and feed the VPT transformer that emits actions a0 to a2. Small embedding strips and game screenshots carry the data.
